task.goal: Compile a governed Carousel harness contract for the 'Cult-Brand' psychological-listicle carousel format: an 11-slide Instagram/social documentary that teaches audience-growth psychology principles through a tarot-card-styled bias reveal, without generating any final slide media.
task.success_condition: Builder ingest/build/export round-trips cleanly with category_id='carousels' preserved, all seven activative_input semantic refs and evidence_provenance_refs preserved as real attestation, and wrong_reading_locks surviving unmodified into the compiled category_binding.
task.atomic_boundary: One ratified carousel reference set (CAR-LST-Cultbrand-3-4-11: cover, hook, seven bias-card slides, weekly action-plan recap, and repost CTA) becomes one structural Builder contract; no per-slide image or copy generation happens inside this harness-authoring step.

source_expression_moment.description: The specific real hook or premise moment this carousel run is being generated from at runtime -- e.g. which of the seven psychological biases (Curiosity Gap, Social Currency, Contrast Effect, Loss Aversion, Authority Hack, Dopamine Scheduling, Pattern Interruption), or which cover-hook variant, is being expressed in this pass.

voice_context.description: The creator/brand voice register this carousel must speak in at runtime -- tone, platform norms, and persona cues (e.g. direct, punchy, dark-humor growth-marketing voice, first-person authority). Distinct from identity_dna_ref: this is a lightweight runtime tone descriptor, not the upstream identity artifact itself.

activative_input.hidden_pressure: The reader already suspects their content underperforms for reasons outside their control (luck, the algorithm) and fears the real explanation is a skill in reading an audience's psychology that they haven't been taught.
activation_directions: map it to your own content
activative_input.stance: Blunt, insider, lightly dark-humored authority -- 'here's what the top 1% of creators know that you don't.'
stakes: not reading as manipulative or cult-like without the intended irony
identity_urges: be seen as in-the-know rather than lucky
avoid looking like an amateur who relies on chance
activative_input.participation_design: One psychological bias revealed per slide via a tarot-card reveal (rank, suit, illustration, and an oracle-style tagline), closing on a seven-day action-plan calendar and an explicit repost call-to-action.
activative_input.intended_reaction: The viewer saves or reposts the carousel and commits to applying one named bias per post over the following week.
activative_input.smallest_useful_commitment: Pick one bias card from the recap slide and write one hook using it today.
wrong_reading_locks: Do not literalize the cult/occult/tarot imagery (masks, hooded robes, oracle cards) into an endorsement of real cult indoctrination, occult practice, or fortune-telling -- it is a metaphorical hook device for teaching audience-psychology principles in content marketing, not literal ideological or spiritual content.

Do not read 'hijacking human psychology' as license to fabricate false personal claims, invented credentials, or fake statistics inside generated hooks -- the bracketed template examples (e.g. '[X]', 'the $50K mistake') are fill-in-the-blank prompts for the creator's own true story, not scripts to populate with invented facts presented as real.

Do not escalate the horror-poster red-spatter cover treatment into actual graphic violence, gore, or extremist/hate-group visual signaling -- the blood-red palette and masked-figure motif is a stylized genre reference (horror-movie-poster aesthetic), not a literal depiction of violence or a real-world extremist symbol.

Do not treat the numbered 'Bias #' slides as targeting instructions against a real, identifiable individual or a vulnerable audience segment -- the tactics (loss aversion, authority hack, etc.) are meant to be applied to the creator's own copywriting choices, not deployed against a named person.

Do not read the closing 'repost this' CTA as license to reproduce or impersonate the on-camera creator (@marketingharry) in future generations -- his on-camera appearance is brand-specific personal likeness, not a reusable template character for other creators' output.
